label: King
summary: The sovereign. The kingdom is his — stored as pledge 'king' on a Person.
quote: The sovereign. The kingdom is his.

label: Regent
summary: Administers the kingdom for the King, and is the catch-basin: every undelegated fief lands on the Regent's desk. Stored as pledge 'steward'.
quote: the catch-basin: every undelegated fief lands on the Regent's desk

label: Vassal
summary: An internal subject, eligible to hold fiefs and hamlets by grant.
quote: An internal subject. Eligible to hold fiefs and hamlets by grant.

label: Squire
summary: Pledged to a person, not a fief — pre-hire, in training, travels with their knight.
quote: Pledged to a *person*, not a fief. Pre-hire; in training; travels with their knight.

label: Artisan
summary: External — contractor, vendor, outside counsel of an outside guild. Can run land (as keeper), can never hold it, and may never head a Crown office. Stored as pledge 'sellsword'.
quote: External — contractor, vendor, outside counsel, of an outside GUILD.

label: Fief (territory kind)
summary: Land, held by a lord, worked by knights — a group's book of doors, holding TerritoryKind 'fief'.
quote: a group's book of doors: land, held by a lord, worked by knights.

label: Hamlet (territory kind)
summary: A lesser holding inside a fief, led on the line of trade by a mayor.
quote: a lesser holding inside a fief.

label: Office (territory kind)
summary: A CROWN OFFICE, seated in the palace and never on land — a place in the record only so a Chancellor's seat is a grant like any other, revocable the same way.
quote:
It is a place in the
 *    record only so a Chancellor's seat is a grant like any other, revocable the
 *    same way

label: Guild
summary: An outside trade the Crown does not staff — roofers, lenders, counsel; its hands are artisans.
quote: an OUTSIDE trade (roofers, lenders, counsel)

label: Garrison
summary: Artisans stationed in a territory — worked land without local leadership.
quote: artisans stationed in a territory

label: Lorded (fief state)
summary: An internal vassal holds the fief by explicit grant. Green, healthy.
quote: States are always computed from the records, never

label: In stewardship (fief state)
summary: No grant, no appointment, nothing recorded — falls to the Regent, red, the state the system hunts.
quote: This is the state the system hunts.

label: Held in plurality (fief state)
summary: One vassal holds several fiefs, each by explicit grant — legitimate and historically normal, watched but not flagged as debt.
quote:
Legitimate
   and historically normal. Watched, not flagged.

label: In regency (fief state)
summary: No vassal lord, but a recorded keeper (an artisan formally appointed) runs the fief day-to-day — the kingdom's work gets done, but by foreign hands. Amber.
quote:
The kingdom's work gets done, but
   by foreign hands. Amber.

label: Garrison posting (record)
summary: Stations an artisan in a territory as workforce — not authority.
quote: Garrison posting** — stations an artisan in a territory as workforce.

label: Fealty (record)
summary: Records a vassal serving inside a fief under its lord.
quote: Fealty** — records a vassal serving inside a fief under its lord.

label: The Regent's desk
summary: Every fief in stewardship appears here as open delegation debt; regencies appear beneath as watch items. Ideal length is zero.
quote: Every fief in stewardship appears on the Regent's desk as an open item of delegation debt.

label: Grant (record)
summary: Places an internal vassal in charge of a territory. Three senses on the same two stored roles: lord on a fief, mayor on a hamlet, lord on an office (a Chancellor's seat).
quote:
Places an internal vassal in charge of a territory. THREE senses, all
 *  carried by the same two stored roles

label: Keeper appointment (record)
summary: Formally names an artisan the keeper of a lordless territory — what makes a regency a regency and not stewardship.
quote: Formally names an artisan the keeper of a lordless territory

label: Arrival (record)
summary: Something new logged at the border — the Marches' entry point, dated.

label: Dispatch (record)
summary: The deliberate act of assigning an arrival to a territory.
quote: The deliberate act of assigning an arrival to a territory.

label: Turnaway (record)
summary: The deliberate act of refusing an arrival at the border.
quote: The deliberate act of refusing an arrival at the border.

label: The Marches
summary: The border lands: work that has arrived in the kingdom but has not yet been assigned to any fief, computed from disposition records like a fief's state.
quote: The Marches: the border lands.

label: The border scribe
summary: Reads raw text logged at the border against the census, recognizes census names, flags unknown name-shaped lists, and pre-fills a destination when it can — deliberately conservative.
quote: the scribe reads the raw text against the census — law 2 made mechanism.

label: The border book
summary: The vault's border_arrivals table, the only door an outside producer will ever write through; folded into the doc's arrivals on every read and marked absorbed once written.
quote:
`border_arrivals`, the **only door an
outside producer will ever write through**.

label: The vault
summary: The chronicle's master copy, a Supabase Postgres behind its own locked door — row security enabled with no policies, so only the secret key passes.
quote:
The chronicle's master copy now rests in a **Supabase
Postgres**

label: The chronicle
summary: The kingdom's mutable record books bound into one volume — the event log and every act, stored as data/chronicle.json in the repo and mirrored to the vault.
quote: The kingdom's mutable record books

label: The tenant (economy) setting
summary: The mechanism by which a deployment overrides the seed tenant's demo fee rates, spend caps and GL chart with its own, without any real figure living in the repository.

label: Upkeep
summary: The recurring monthly cost of the kingdom's structure — retainers, salaries, subscriptions, dues; each line may name the territory that bears it and the person who receives it.
quote: retainers, salaries, subscriptions, dues

label: The estates in trust (the AppFolio dimension)
summary: The rents, deposits, work-order costs, and owner draws of the Patrons' estates — the Patrons' coin, not the Crown's; the Crown only holds and moves it, per estate and per door.
quote:
This is fiduciary money: a
new book of **estate ledgers**

label: The Crown's own coin (the QuickBooks dimension)
summary: The company's own money — the fees it earns for keeping the estates (tribute), against its upkeep; the money that decides whether the kingdom falls.
quote:
the money that decides
whether **the kingdom falls**

label: The fee bridge
summary: A management/leasing/markup fee is simultaneously an expense to an owner in trust and revenue to the company, carried across by the mirrored Due-to-Mgmt / Due-from-Trust clearing pair.
quote: The two worlds meet at exactly one hinge — the fee bridge

label: Coffers (reading)
summary: The unified reading of tribute per retained door against upkeep — the fail state (kingdom falls) is a reading, coffers trending below zero, never an invented number.
quote: export interface Coffers {

label: FeeRule
summary: A percentage in basis points or a flat cents amount that feeAmount applies to a basis to compute a fee, then records as a money event.
quote: Fees are computed, then recorded as an amount.

label: BudgetLine
summary: A working-fluid monthly plan for the Crown's own book, measured against the actuals folded from the money log by readBudgetVsActual.
quote: A working-fluid monthly plan for the Crown's own book

label: The owner-approval spend gate
summary: True when a repair cost is at or above the economy's threshold and so needs owner approval before the vendor proceeds — the recon's "$400 cap" generalized.
quote:
the recon's "$400
cap" / the grammars' "NTE

label: MoneyEvent
summary: The money-dimension record — an append-only event recording what happened and to whom; the balanced debit/credit postings are derived from it on every read, never stored.
quote: A money event records *what happened and to whom*

label: EconomyBook
summary: The two-book chart (trust and corporate), fee rules, spend caps and budget — a loadable static book like the catalog, working-fluid at founding.
quote: a loadable static book (working-fluid founding chart

label: Compliance check (reading)
summary: Five live trust-accounting guardrails folded from the postings: the aggregate-liability identity, no overdrawn trust bank, no overdrawn owner, deposits held whole, earned fees swept in time.
quote:
the **aggregate-liability identity** (the bank reconciles), **no trust bank overdrawn**, **no
owner overdrawn**

label: The Office of Works
summary: Maintenance — keeping the buildings sound. Headed by the Chancellor of Works.
quote: Maintenance — keeping the buildings sound

label: The Office of Tenancy
summary: Leasing — filling doors and keeping tenants. Headed by the Chancellor of Tenancy.
quote: Leasing — filling doors and keeping tenants

label: The Chancery
summary: The administrative layer: the books, records, payments, and law. Legal folds in here; headed by the Chancellor of the Chancery.
quote: The administrative layer: the books, records, payments, and law

label: FOUNDING_GUILDS still names Crown offices, not outside trades
summary: The code's Guild/GuildReading/FOUNDING_GUILDS types now hold the three Crown offices (Works, Tenancy, Chancery), not outside trades — the header names this a stale, unfinished rename, load-bearing across a pinned map contract.

the rename is in progress and the names are

label: The catalog tree — domain, system, leaf
summary: A task-type is a word reached by walking domain to system to leaf; the dotted key is the stable identifier an event references.
quote: A **task-type** is a word in a bounded, compositional language.

label: CatalogRow
summary: A task-type row: key, title, class, mode, domain/system facets, and an optional completes binding to the FlowTemplate that finishes it.

label: FlowTemplate

summary: One step of a flow: a catalog row, a holder, a board, a timing edge, an optional SLA, an optional repeat and condition.

label: The event log
summary: The sole record of the real work; a work item, a queue, who holds the ball, aging, a KPI are all readings folded from it, never stored state.
quote: The event log — the living instrument's spine

label: The human-in-the-loop event arc
summary: proposed → awaiting → approved / overridden — the clerk layer's arc: an agent proposes and waits, a human ratifies or overrides.
quote: 'proposed' // an agent proposes an act and waits on a human

label: The Throne
summary: The King's seat — a fusion of the org's delegation debt (fiefs with no lord) and the work's delegation debt (cases on no real seat) into one number.
quote: The sovereign's top-down reading over the whole kingdom

label: RealmReading (a score, not a place)
summary: The Regent's whole-kingdom fusion — pods, guilds, unseated work and coffers into the debt he drives to zero. Deliberately not renamed despite sharing five letters with tenure.ts's Realm.
quote:
The `RealmReading` below is a
// SCORE — the Regent's whole-kingdom fusion, the debt he drives to zero.

label: The clerk fleet
summary: One agent per seat, each a bounded task and a run that works through the real flow engine and stops at a judgment, proposed and awaiting the Regent.
quote: an agent on every seat

label: The consequence engine
summary: Severity, faith, withdrawal and the coffers trend, all folded from age and inaction against the clock — the fail state is a reading, not stored.
quote:
records-in,
readings-out

label: Patron
summary: An owner who has entrusted their estate to the Crown's keeping and pays tribute for it; faith starts at 100, eroded by the severities on their doors.
quote: export interface PatronReading {

label: Pod
summary: A knight's book of business — a set of owners (Patrons) and their doors (the land); the top-level holding the metaphor was missing.
quote:
a knight's book of business:
// a set of OWNERS (the Patrons) and their DOORS (the LAND)

label: War Game
summary: A generated synthetic operation at scale, poured through the operator, with a simulated clock the Regent can advance to watch queues fill and drain.
quote: A full simulation of the operating model

label: Scenario (the muster library's recipe shape)
summary: A recipe — a seed plus a declared shape — re-dealt against whatever the setting is; never a dumped event log, so a rename never butchers it.
quote: A SCENARIO is a recipe, never a recording.

label: The grand muster
summary: The torture-test scenario — a whole operation dealt at once, structurally insolvent from deploy on purpose; the stress test that proved the fleet, the Ledger and the economy.
quote: the grand muster stays, unchanged, as the stress test.

label: The Intro Campaign, "A Small Holding"
summary: A small, clean, solvent-at-rest scenario of six acts teaching the causal loop: neglect drops faith drops tribute drops solvency, delegation holds it.
quote: Shape: small, clean, solvent-at-rest, and staged.

label: Edict (crown edicts, tenure hierarchy)
summary: A realm's own regulatory obligation — licence status, CE hours, disclosure, trust-account rules, filing deadlines. Data model only; no UI built yet.
quote:
over the real
obligations: licence
status, CE hours, disclosure, trust-account rules, filing deadlines.

label: The census
summary: The founding document, ratified and dated — adopted into the chronicle once, shelf by shelf, and never consulted again for the present.
quote:
the census below is the founding
document, adopted into the chronicle once and never consulted again for the present.

label: The court
summary: Where the deliberate acts are made and struck; the living records reside in the chronicle in two adopted books — the acts book and the census book.
quote: The court: where the deliberate acts are made and struck.

summary: A fief folded to its state, holder, grant, appointment, any stray grants, its hamlets, vassals, and garrison — the reading the board renders.
